home.title: Modern Nuxt starter for public websites
home.lead: Nuxt Modern Starter brings marketing pages, auth flows, multilingual content, SEO routes, and Docker/Nginx deployment defaults into one clean foundation. Use it to launch a SaaS website, product frontend, or content hub, then replace content and backend integrations as your product grows.
home.featuresTitle: The usual public-site building blocks, already organized
home.featuresLead: Inspired by the Nuxt SaaS Template hierarchy, the homepage now gives the hero section a stronger follow-through with product-ready feature cards.

design.title: Unified design system
design.description: Built on Ant Design Vue and local theme tokens so color mode, radius, shadows, and spacing stay consistent.

i18n.title: Localized routing
i18n.description: Language prefixes, switching, and localized links are ready for marketing pages and content routes.

seo.title: SEO-friendly pages
seo.description: Home, pricing, help, and article pages all have extensible SEO entry points for public indexing.

auth.title: Account flows
auth.description: Login, registration, and account pages are wired to basic state and ready for a real backend.

content.title: Content hub
content.description: FAQ comes from typed local config; news and pricing load through the public API and can later move to a CMS or backend.

deploy.title: Production deployment
deploy.description: Docker, Nginx, SWR route rules, and security headers are already part of the starter.

workflow.title: A shorter path from starter to launch
workflow.lead: It keeps the starter lightweight while adding the capability, conversion, and content structure a SaaS frontend needs.

steps.routes: Reuse home, pricing, help, and news pages to organize public information first.
steps.content: Replace i18n copy and content sources next (pricing/news already use the API and can move to a CMS).
steps.auth: Connect your backend account system when you are ready to wire sessions, roles, and the product app.

home.ctaTitle: Use this Nuxt foundation to launch a polished product frontend faster.

about.title: Built for public sites and lightweight SaaS frontends
about.lead: Nuxt Modern Starter is a reusable Nuxt 4 foundation for marketing pages, content hubs, and optional auth-ready product surfaces.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.body: We organize the most common public-site capabilities—i18n routing, SEO, content pages, auth samples, and deployment patterns—into a runnable starting point so teams can focus on product differences instead of rebuilding infrastructure.

items.focus: Stay focused on public-site scenarios with clear module boundaries instead of an oversized starter.
items.quality: Ship with TypeScript strict mode, linting, tests, and deployment samples from day one.
items.openness: Keep public and product layers separate so local content and API-driven content can be swapped in gradually.

paragraphs.origin: The starter comes from repeated needs across SaaS websites and product frontends: marketing home, pricing, help, news, sign-in/sign-up, plus logged-in workspace and editor examples.
paragraphs.practice: It defaults to Chinese as the primary locale with English under /en, mixes SSR/prerender/SWR for public pages, and keeps product routes language-neutral with CSR rendering.
paragraphs.next: If you are evaluating a Nuxt public-site template, start with the README quick start, then replace copy, content, and backend integrations for your product.

help.title: Learn how to use Nuxt Modern Starter
help.lead: This page collects common questions about project setup, i18n, auth, SEO, and deployment. Quick-start steps and resource lists come from i18n; FAQ comes from local config and can later move to a CMS or backend API.

steps.install: Enable Corepack, then run pnpm install.
steps.dev: Run pnpm dev and browse default Chinese routes plus /en English routes.
steps.explore: Review home, pricing, about, help, and news pages to understand the public-site structure.
steps.extend: Follow docs/usage.md to add pages, requests, SEO, and optional auth.
